summary:
## Project Ignition

**Project Ignition**, is an interactive 3-dimensional space mission game, designed to make rocket engineering and mission planning both fun and educationally based. Users can create their own rockets; develop configurations for testing; launch to low earth orbit, lunar or Martian surfaces; and are subjected to realistic physical forces including thrust, mass, gravity, orbital dynamics and atmospheric effects.

The game was developed from NASA resources and data, converting actual mission obstacles to gameplay. These include management of fuel levels; failure of engines; faulty sensors; loss of communications due to blackouts; and radiation exposure along with harsh landing conditions. The combination of creative spacecraft design (and its limitations) creates **Project Ignition**, which will build users' curiosity about space travel; provide users with scientific knowledge; and improve problem solving abilities in addition to providing entertainment through learning.
details:
Project Ignition functions as a tool for users to design their own rockets, test different configurations, and launch missions to reach orbit around the Earth or land on the moon and mars. Using realistic physics (thrust, mass, gravitational forces, orbital mechanics, and atmospheric drag) the user's design choices will have a direct effect upon their mission's success.

Using real-life mission problems as part of the gameplay, players will need to deal with issues such as fuel levels, engine failure, faulty sensors, communication black out, radiation exposure, and landing conditions. By using this type of game platform, the developers are creating curiosity, scientific knowledge, and problem solving skills in addition to providing fun and accessable means to explore space.

The Project Ignition development team approached this project from a creative perspective by combining an easy-to-use 3D model builder with real mission based constraints. The team thought about what would be accessible to a wide range of users, how much of an education could they provide through the gameplay process, how realistic could they make the game play, how engaging was the gameplay going to be for users, and where did they want to find that balance between difficulty level and fun factor.
